Two studies (Carr 153 lesions, Simons-Linares 113) contribute about 44% of the data, so the pooled estimate is largely two single centres, and both are from the United States

A pooled specificity of 86% applied to a population in which most cysts are benign generates a large absolute number of false positives; the Fagan plot's 40% pretest assumption is far above the prevalence of mucinous disease among incidental cysts and conceals this

Pseudocysts also have low intracystic glucose and were handled variably across studies, so part of the test's apparent discrimination against 'non-mucinous' lesions depends on how many pseudocysts each cohort contained

33964311.n: 8 studies, 609 lesions; mean patient age 63.56 +/- 2.75 years, 60.36% women, mean lesion size 36.47 +/- 5.60 mm; CEA comparison from 7 studies and 534 lesions; combination testing from 4 studies and 348 lesions
33964311.bottom_line: Establishes that cyst fluid glucose below about 50 mg/dL is more sensitive (91% vs 56%) and more accurate (94% vs 85%) than CEA for calling a cyst mucinous, and that combining the two adds nothing over glucose alone; it does not establish anything about dysplasia grade, and in most contributing studies the reference standard for non-mucinous cysts was the same non-histologic criteria the test was meant to replace.

The panel did not include CDKN2A, despite CDKN2A alterations being found only in IPMNs with advanced neoplasia

The study does not address the optimal way to integrate targeted NGS into surveillance protocols, and no guideline has sufficient accuracy to dictate management
The European evidence-based guidelines could not be applied to the cohort
critique: The allele-frequency rules that lift specificity to 98-100% were derived in this group's earlier single-centre cohorts and are applied here to specimens processed by the same lead institution's laboratory, with the retrospective confirmation cohort drawn from the same molecular archive; this is internal rather than independent validation, and the paper's framing as multi-institutional refers to specimen origin, not to analysis

The guideline comparison is not like for like: AGA and Fukuoka absolute criteria were reconstructed retrospectively from records submitted by 31 sites with unstandardised EUS and local cytology, while PancreaSeq ran prospectively in one centralised CLIA laboratory - the guidelines are judged on degraded inputs and the assay on optimal ones

Verification is partial (251 of 1216 followed patients, 21%) and the decision to operate was informed by the molecular result; this depresses the apparent sensitivity of the guideline criteria and inflates that of the assay, and no analysis attempts to correct for it

'None of the 965 patients who did not undergo surgery developed malignancy' is an absence of events at a median of 23 months, offered in the abstract as a finding; it is uninformative about a lesion with a multi-year dwell time and should not be read as evidence that withholding surgery was safe

The serous cystadenoma and cystic PanNET performance figures rest on 13 and 34 resected cases; the TP53/TERT addition that takes SCA sensitivity from 71% to 100% is 4 patients, and the prognostic LOH analysis pools 34 cystic with 53 solid PanNETs, a different disease presentation, to reach its metastasis estimates

Specificity for advanced neoplasia is computed against all other resected cysts, a group enriched for low-grade IPMN and non-neoplastic lesions by the same referral and resection pathway; the quantity a clinician needs - the proportion of molecularly positive cysts under surveillance that will progress - is not estimated anywhere

The senior authors hold a financial interest in the field being validated (an honorarium from Foundation Medicine, and a royalty interest in the GNAS invention through Thrive Earlier Detection), and the paper is in substance a validation of an assay run by the authors' own laboratory and named by them

Nine resected IPMNs were MAPK/GNAS-negative preoperatively and positive on the specimen, which is a false-negative rate the paper attributes to sampling rather than to the test; if sampling is the limiting factor, the 90% sensitivity is a property of the EUS-FNA as much as of the panel, and that cannot be improved by sequencing
36209796.n: 1933 cyst fluid specimens prospectively tested from 1889 patients at 31 institutions, of which 1887 (98%) from 1832 patients were satisfactory; clinicopathologic follow-up in 1216 patients (66%, 2-35 months, median 21-23); surgical pathology in 251 (21%), of which 246 were pancreatic cysts; plus a retrospective confirmation cohort of 97 (63 mucinous, 34 non-mucinous, 22 with advanced neoplasia) and 87 PanNETs (34 cystic, 53 solid biopsies)

Despite the prospective nature of the institutional databases, retrospective assessment of data collected over 30 years carries variability in feature definitions and in patient management, only partly offset by large numbers and long follow-up
The relatively limited follow-up of surveilled patients

Mural nodule size was not available, forcing use of the 2012 rather than 2017 IAP definitions
Patients' data were extracted from each centre's institutional database and in most cases had already been included in prior publications

critique: The reassuring standardised incidence ratios rest on almost no events: 2 cancers in the Trivial <=15 mm group and 3 in the >=75-year group, giving intervals of 0.10-3.36 and 0.23-3.39 that remain compatible with a threefold excess risk; 'comparable to the general population' is a failure to exclude harm, not a demonstration of safety, and the paper's recommendations are phrased as though it were the latter

The SIR falls with age not because older patients are safer but because the population comparator's pancreatic cancer incidence rises steeply with age - a mechanism the paper states explicitly and then uses to justify stopping surveillance in exactly the group whose absolute risk is highest

The question is what happens after 5 years, but the cohort's median surveillance is 53 months and even the Trivial subgroup's median is 85 months - roughly 2.5 years of observation past the 5-year mark, against the 10-15-year horizons over which Pergolini and Oyama located their events; the paper's own limitation about 'relatively limited follow-up' is doing more work than its placement suggests

164 patients were resected and 843 developed WF or HRS and thereby left the low-risk state, so the denominator for 'no excess risk' is continuously purged of progressors while the person-time they contributed before progressing stays in; this is the same structural issue as in the papers the study argues against, applied in the opposite direction

Malignancy ascertainment was not systematic: 14 of 40 cancers were diagnosed radiologically or by FNA rather than pathologically, and patients lost to follow-up across 12 centres in 8 countries are nowhere accounted for; unascertained cancers bias the SIR numerator downward, which is the direction that favours the conclusion

The authors contrast their result with Oyama's SIR of 6.7 in cysts under 15 mm and attribute the difference to their added 5-year stability criterion, but the two cohorts differ in country, baseline worrisome-feature status, pathology practice, EUS-FNA use and ascertainment method, so the comparison does not isolate stability as the explanation

Of the patients in this 'low-risk' cohort who were eventually resected, 31.8% overall and 38.1% of those resected after 5 years had high-grade dysplasia or invasive cancer; that is the yield of the resections the surveillance programme triggered, and it indicates that when these cysts do declare themselves they are frequently already advanced - a finding that sits uneasily beside the recommendation to stop looking

Three of the senior authors are among the authors of the Kyoto guidelines that adopted the stopping option this paper supports, and the lead centre's prior publications supplied much of the cohort, so the evidence and the guideline it informs are not independent
37406887.n: 3844 patients with presumed BD-IPMN included from 4356 screened (median age 66, IQR 15; 60.2% female; median initial diameter 12 mm, IQR 9; median surveillance 53 months, IQR 53); 1617 (42%) developed no WF or HRS in the first 5 years ('Trivial BD-IPMN'), of whom 762 (47.1%) had a cyst <=15 mm at 5 years; 164 (4.3%) resected
37406887.bottom_line: In the largest multicentre surveillance cohort of presumed branch-duct IPMN without worrisome features, cysts stable for 5 years carried a pancreatic cancer incidence no higher than the age-matched population in patients over 75 with cysts under 30 mm, or over 65 with cysts <=15 mm, supporting selective discontinuation; with only 2-3 cancers in those subgroups, incomplete ascertainment and a median of roughly 2.5 years of observation past the 5-year mark, it cannot exclude a clinically meaningful late risk.

limitations: The method provides no training in the technical aspects of performing a high-quality EUS-nCLE examination
The teaching module and targeted feedback came from a single nCLE expert, which may limit reproducibility, although prerecorded feedback has been shown non-inferior to real-time feedback

Training and competency assessment used edited high-yield videos acquired by experts, removing technique variability, which may have produced higher accuracy than would be expected in clinical practice; results may not generalise to real-time procedures by novice operators
Observer selection bias from including only US early-career endosonographers recruited by email and social media
Patient selection bias is inherent in using videos of common cysts with validated nCLE patterns and confirmed histopathology
Unmeasured confounders such as prior exposure to or knowledge of nCLE and variable motivation to learn may partly explain the inefficacy of the refresher intervention
Learning curves were not formally assessed for each cyst subtype
Training in differentiating the degree of dysplasia within IPMNs was not evaluated
Interruptions and lack of nCLE exposure longer than 8 weeks might cause decrements in competency, which was not tested

The senior author designed the teaching module, chose and edited the high-yield clips, delivered all the feedback, co-selected the participants and is a speaker for the device manufacturer; there is no independent reference reader or blinded adjudication anywhere in the design

Prevalence in the video set is engineered at 66% mucinous, so the reported accuracy figures are not transportable to a clinic where most cysts are benign, and no PPV or NPV is given at any realistic prevalence

37473969.n: 21 early-career nCLE-naive endosonographers (10 advanced endoscopy fellows, 11 practising advanced endoscopists; 86% academic), each assessing 80 nCLE videos twice; videos from 80 patients with confirmed histopathology - 53 mucinous (37 IPMN, 16 MCN) and 27 non-mucinous (11 SCA, 3 pseudocyst, 13 cystic NET/SPN)

The cut-off value of mural nodule size for diagnosing HGD/IC remains controversial, and the presence of a mural nodule alone does not always have high impact on prediction
Thickened or enhancing cyst wall is an ambiguous factor whose measurement methods and predictive cut-off have not been established
Definitions of 'new onset' and 'acute exacerbation' of diabetes have not yet been determined
'Increase in size of MPD' is expected to predict aggressive behaviour but evidence on this dynamic issue is lacking, so it was not included as a worrisome feature
Nomogram limitations include lack of distinction between branch-duct and main-duct IPMN in some models, small numbers of resected IPMNs in some countries or regions, and lack of external validation
Accuracy of diagnosis of pancreatic cystic lesions is only 47-78% and of HGD/IC prediction 73-97%
The necessity of long-term surveillance remains unclear and will be determined by regional health economics, the risk of concomitant PDAC and patient age, condition, life expectancy and preference

T1 substaging per the Verona consensus has been followed by few reports to date and its clinical meaning, especially for the T1 subgroups, must be validated in future; a unique T stage for IPMN with invasive carcinoma remains a challenge

critique: n is null, and the resected-series rates of 31% and 62% high-grade dysplasia or invasive carcinoma remain the quantitative backbone of the risk framework; although this version states plainly that the true rate across all branch-duct IPMNs is much lower, it does not supply that denominator, so the criteria are still calibrated on operated specimens

The two-option recommendation on stopping surveillance after 5 years is a recorded disagreement rather than a finding: the text says most Japanese physicians accept the low progression risk but remain concerned about concomitant PDAC, and the guideline resolves this by permitting either course at SIGN grade C. A pathway built on this cannot claim evidential support for whichever option it adopts

The geographic dependence of the concomitant PDAC rate is stated explicitly - most such studies come from Japan, where the whole gland is sectioned at 5 mm and clinicians are primed to look for it, while elsewhere the risk resembles the general population's - yet the 0.4-1.0% yearly figure and the 3- to 5-fold relative risk are then applied globally without adjustment for where a reader practises

The thresholds that changed did so on weak grounds: 2.5 mm per year replaces 5 mm per 2 years because 2.5 was 'reported most frequently' among values spanning 0.96-3.5 mm per year, and new-onset diabetes enters as a worrisome feature on risk ratios of 1.27 and 1.61 with no agreed definition of 'new onset' - the guideline says so and adopts it anyway

The thresholds that did not change were retained after the same text reports that a mural nodule of 5 mm or more carries an odds ratio of only 1.19-3.16 and MPD of 10 mm or more 1.06-1.76 in the newest multivariable models, and that a 10 mm nodule discriminates far better (odds ratio 7.90 versus 2.93); keeping the 5 mm and 10 mm lines 'because of lack of evidence strongly supporting these revisions' preserves criteria that the cited evidence undercuts, and places the burden of proof on change rather than on the status quo

Bringing EUS and EUS-FNA cytology inside the high-risk-stigmata assessment makes the risk classification depend on an operator-dependent test the same document says cannot be performed at the same level everywhere, and on a cytology with 28.7% overall sensitivity - so a negative result carries almost no weight while a positive one becomes an absolute surgical indication, an asymmetry never stated

No sensitivity, specificity or predictive values are reported for the revised high-risk-stigmata and worrisome-feature lists as a whole, three guideline generations after the framework was introduced; the surveillance protocol is stratified at 20 and 30 mm, and Hamada's subsequent validation in a 3336-patient cohort found risk well separated at 20 mm but not at 30 mm, so one of the two thresholds in the new protocol does not stratify

Surgical mortality and morbidity are again absent from the entire document, as is any cost-effectiveness estimate, even though health economics is invoked as a reason to consider stopping surveillance and as the framing for the whole discontinuation question

Zelga's additive worrisome-feature figures (22%, 34%, 59% and 100%) are quoted as a single study without sample sizes or confidence intervals, and a 100% rate with 4 or more features is the kind of small-cell result that does not survive replication; it is nonetheless the basis for recommending nomogram-assisted surgical decisions

Eleven authors, several of whom also authored the five commissioned systematic reviews and the validation cohorts cited, and the Kyoto working group overlaps substantially with the 2012 and 2017 Fukuoka groups whose criteria are being revised; no conflict-of-interest statement appears in this text extraction
38182527.bottom_line: The current international guideline, which brought EUS and EUS-FNA cytology inside the risk classification, simplified surveillance into three size strata, adopted a 2.5 mm/year growth rate and new-onset diabetes as worrisome features, separated intraductal oncocytic papillary neoplasm from IPMN, and for the first time offered the option of stopping surveillance for a stable cyst under 20 mm at 5 years; that stopping option is presented as one of two permissible courses at SIGN grade C, no operating characteristics are given for the risk tiers, and the malignancy rates behind the whole framework remain resected-series prevalences.

limitations: The malignancy risk of the most common cystic lesions - IPMN and MCN - remains poorly understood because of a paucity of natural history data and the difficulty of estimating the true population prevalence
Much of the current literature is limited by selection bias, and long-term prospective comparative effectiveness trials evaluating observation versus resection are lacking

Published studies are limited by incongruous use of definitions: 'malignant' may mean only invasive adenocarcinoma, or high-grade dysplasia, or both, and the criteria for a 'positive' cytology vary, with some studies using cytology only and others the presence of mucin or CEA above 192 ng/mL

The increasing incidence of cysts does not represent an increase in prevalence but detection bias from increased imaging use; although resources spent on diagnosis, surveillance and treatment have increased over two decades, the number of patients diagnosed with and surviving pancreatic adenocarcinoma has not changed
Available studies lack patient-centred factors such as underlying genetic risk, behaviours and comorbidity, and most patients with pancreatic cysts die of another cause
Cyst histologic subtype is often not considered or available when predicting malignant transformation and likely plays a role in prognosis

There is a paucity of data on the ability of cross-sectional imaging to diagnose small (<10 mm) cysts independently of further evaluation, and even EUS-FNA occasionally fails to give a definitive diagnosis in diminutive cysts because of the limited analyses possible on small fluid samples; most cysts are small when discovered, so both patient and provider are left with diagnostic ambiguity
Guidelines that refrain from time-based surveillance recommendations acknowledge insufficient knowledge of the natural history of the cyst and of the patient
critique: n is null and this is a narrative review by three authors with no systematic search, no inclusion criteria and no quality appraisal; its Table 1 assigns malignant potential to each cyst type - 'very minimal', 'minimal', 'moderate' - explicitly 'based on author consensus', which is expert opinion presented in the typographic form of data and is likely to be cited as such

The five long-term branch-duct IPMN series in Table 2 are placed in a single column of 'rate of transformation' at 3.5-5.5% despite having structurally incompatible denominators: Pergolini's 20 of 363 is restricted to patients already observed beyond 5 years, Oyama's 30 of 804 is a competing-risk figure in a five-year survivor subset, and Crippa's 5 of 144 is a non-operative cohort selected for having worrisome features. The apparent agreement across countries and designs is an artefact of tabulating quantities that do not measure the same thing

The statement that branch-duct IPMN without worrisome features carries a risk 'similar to the general population' is taken from Marchegiani 2023, where that conclusion rests on 2 to 3 cancers in the relevant subgroups with confidence intervals reaching above 3; the review repeats the point estimate without the interval, and never sets it against Oyama's 6.7-fold standardised incidence ratio in cysts under 15 mm, which appears in its own Table 2

The cost arguments are presented without reconciliation: $3.6 million per cancer detected and $171,143 per QALY are used to frame surveillance as poor value, while a $20,096 per QALY figure for the same disease sits two paragraphs later, and the review does not explain that the two models differ in cyst size, guideline, era and assumptions

The claim that specificity above 67% for high-grade dysplasia or cancer would make surveillance cost-effective, and 'may be achieved' with NGS, adopts a threshold from a single Markov model and a test whose own validation studies tuned their allele-frequency rules in-sample and were conducted by a single laboratory

The population-versus-individual framing is offered as the crux of the controversy but no quantities are attached to either side - no estimate of how many cancers a stopping rule would miss, nor of how many operations and MRIs indefinite surveillance would add - so the central argument of the review is conducted without numbers

The review opens by observing that spending on cyst surveillance has risen steeply without changing pancreatic adenocarcinoma mortality, which is the strongest available argument that current surveillance does not work; it then describes surveillance strategies at length without returning to that observation, and the figure it uses to illustrate the opposite case is a single patient who progressed after choosing surveillance over completion pancreatectomy

The guideline comparison table reproduces several criteria inaccurately - for example listing the ACR high-risk stigma as 'MPD <10 mm' and a worrisome feature as 'MPD >7 cm' - so a reader using the table rather than the source documents may be misled about what each guideline requires
38442782.bottom_line: A current narrative review that lays out cyst types, the diagnostic armamentarium and a side-by-side comparison of the five major guidelines, and frames surveillance cessation as a population-versus-individual trade-off; it establishes no new evidence, its malignancy estimates by cyst type are explicitly the authors' consensus, and its tabulated branch-duct transformation rates pool incompatible denominators into an apparent agreement.
38442782.funding: None; the authors disclose no conflicts

limitations: The centre's surveillance protocol was not necessarily based on the revised Kyoto guidelines; surveillance was more intense for low-risk IPMNs, with imaging continued at 6- to 12-month intervals, so prospective data are needed on the risk-benefit balance of guideline-compliant surveillance
The cohort was established at a single tertiary care centre and a selection bias should be considered
There might be unaccounted confounding factors, although the findings were not materially altered by adjusting for major patient characteristics

A majority of participants were Japanese and the proportion of concomitant PDAC identified during long-term surveillance was relatively high, which may understate the predictive ability of the Kyoto criteria for carcinoma incidence
Rare parameters such as a caliber change of the MPD and IPMN wall thickening were too infrequent for robust statistical assessment

Further research is needed on the optimal cut-off values of predictive factors - CA19-9 for incidence, and IPMN size for both prevalence and incidence - and the null findings for high CA19-9 and size >=30 mm may be due to unvalidated cut-offs; risk was clearly stratified at 20 mm but not at 30 mm
critique: An odds ratio of 2269 with a confidence interval from 310 to 16,600 is a separation artefact: the no-risk-factor stratum contained a single event among 2189 patients, so the model is fitting a near-empty cell, and reporting the figure as an effect size in the abstract misleads about what was measured

The short-term analysis is a prevalence study in which the exposures - a mural nodule, a dilated duct, positive cytology, jaundice - are themselves the triggers for the work-up that finds the carcinoma; the odds ratios therefore quantify how well the criteria select patients for investigation rather than how well they predict disease, and nothing in the design separates the two

The long-term analysis excludes anyone diagnosed with carcinoma or resected within 6 months, which strips prevalent cancers from the numerator while retaining their risk factors in the denominator, and the worrisome-feature analyses additionally exclude all HRS-positive patients, so the 0/1/2/3-4 feature gradient is measured in a cohort already purged of its highest-risk members

Half the events (68 of 138) were concomitant PDACs, and the worrisome-feature gradient holds only for IPMN-derived carcinoma (P for heterogeneity .002); the criteria therefore validate prediction of the lesion they describe and not of the cancer that accounts for half the carcinoma diagnoses and presents at a metastatic stage three times as often

Derived versus concomitant adjudication in this report rests on imaging continuity and histological transition without molecular confirmation, unlike the same group's 2020 analysis, so the split that carries the main biological conclusion is the least verifiable quantity in the paper

The cohort is the same University of Tokyo prospective database, over overlapping years, as Oyama 2020, with shared authors and an overlapping patient set; this is a re-analysis of a known cohort rather than external validation of the Kyoto criteria, and four members of the Kyoto working group are at this institution

The 2.7% and 6.1% post-five-year incidences bear directly on the guideline's stop-or-continue option, but they come from a centre that surveilled more intensively than the guideline advises - the authors say so - so they are an upper bound on what can be detected, not an estimate of what a guideline-compliant programme would find

Risk was not stratified at the 30 mm threshold that the Kyoto guidelines use to set the shortest surveillance interval, with the >=30 mm hazard ratio (1.75, 1.00-3.08) lower than that for 20-29 mm (2.07); the paper attributes this to an unvalidated cut-off rather than treating it as a failure of the criterion it set out to validate

No sensitivity, specificity or predictive values for the revised HRS/WF classification as a whole appear in the main text - they are relegated to supplementary tables - so a clinician cannot read off what the criteria rule in or out, only relative hazards
38880125.n: 3336 patients in the whole cohort for short-term analyses (3041 branch-duct, 271 mixed-type, 24 main-duct; baseline risk level none 2189, worrisome features 997, high-risk stigmata 150) and 3179 in the long-term cohort (none 2185, WF 960, HRS 34), with 22,339 person-years and a median follow-up of 6.2 years (range 0.5-23.6)
38880125.bottom_line: The first large validation of the revised Kyoto criteria, establishing that they stratify both carcinoma prevalence (49% with high-risk stigmata vs 1.3% with worrisome features vs 0.05% with neither) and long-term incidence, with risk rising stepwise to a tenfold hazard at 3-4 worrisome features; it does not validate the guideline's surveillance protocol or its 30 mm threshold, the gradient holds only for IPMN-derived and not concomitant carcinoma, and the cohort overlaps the same centre's earlier series rather than providing external validation.
